paragraphs: The Big Dinosaur, posted by Lily. On Saturday morning, the Explorers visited the science museum. We arrived at ten past nine, and many families were already inside. Guide Ann met us at the door and took us on a short tour. Mia took the photos, and I wrote this page. Here are the facts about the biggest star of the museum.

The dinosaur is a model, and it stands in the main hall. It is twelve meters long and four meters high. Its tail alone is five meters long, and its neck is three meters long. Each tooth is as long as my hand. Visitors can walk under its tail. Mia stood next to one leg, and she looked very small. The model came to the museum three years ago. "The real animal lived a very long time ago," said Guide Ann. "It ate plants, not meat."

The museum is open from nine o'clock to five o'clock every day except Monday. A ticket costs fifty baht for a child and one hundred baht for an adult. A family ticket for four people costs two hundred and fifty baht. You can buy tickets at the door. A baby does not pay. Our group paid only thirty baht for each child. The price is lower for a group, because Teacher Kim asked the museum first.

After the tour, we went to the museum shop. A notice on the door said, "Sale today! Dinosaur guidebook sixty baht." The guidebook usually costs eighty baht, so we were lucky. It has forty pages and twenty photos of dinosaurs. Leo bought one, and I bought one, too. The books look great. I gave the woman at the shop one hundred baht, and she gave me forty baht back.

Behind the museum, there is a garden with small dinosaur models. The sun is strong at noon, and it can burn your skin. If you visit the garden, wear a hat. The garden is free. A bottle of water costs fifteen baht at the garden door. Which dinosaur do you like best? Tell us in a message!
text.summary: Lily writes a page for Explorers' Blog about the dinosaur model in the science museum. The page gives its size, the ticket prices, the guidebook sale, and a safety tip about the sun.
